candidate_relations.rationale: The package-build configuration uses an explicit managed-root allowlist and excludes project knowledge and integration material, strengthening the final-plan requirement to package only generic-framework content rather than the repository wholesale.

The operator-registry contract explicitly states install and bootstrap create no operator authority and requires an initial-root ceremony, strengthening the orchestrator design rule that bootstrap cannot establish authority.

The live-model activation workflow preserves model bytes, prepares an exact activation bundle, and verifies the authority and canonical boundary, strengthening the ingestion-operation separation between evidence preparation and authority-bearing Canon mutation.
Preserving externally supplied live-model bytes before finalization strengthens the raw-candidate preservation principle that evaluation and processing must not rewrite model output.

The workflow tests verify immutable pause acknowledgements, terminal completion, bounded cancellation, and successor revisions, strengthening the contract that one workflow remains bound to immutable authenticated intent.
Recording workflow progression through immutable append-only events strengthens the workflow contract’s immutable bounded-intent lifecycle model.
The grant tests show exact proposal containment, workflow matching, stale-state checks, and materiality pauses constrain issuance, strengthening the bounded grant-operations proposition.
The grant tests explicitly show materiality pauses block approval issuance, strengthening the Human-to-Agent rule that grant authority cannot waive a required materiality acknowledgement.

The grant tests require an exact wholly covered proposal and reject partial, unknown, stale, or scope-mismatched effects, strengthening the common-mutation rule that grant-derived approval binds exactly one immutable proposal and valid basis.
Independent apply-time validation for proposal, basis, state, and domain strengthens the common mutation substrate’s distinction and exact binding of direct and grant-derived approval evidence.

The legacy Steward-setup tests require explicit scope, explicit confirmation, idempotent replay, and prohibit overwriting different authorization, strengthening the Steward-authorization contract’s explicit scope and independent authorization state.
The independent Steward-authorization conformance workflow strengthens the runtime proposition that Steward authorization is a separately testable domain rather than an implicit part of role state.

The immutable release baseline’s package, manifest, transport, installer, validator, schema, source-commit, and content-identity binding strengthens the install-package requirement to persist exact verified release and compatibility metadata.
The release-package builder collects only configured managed files into a deterministic package, strengthening the final-plan rule that the builder use an explicit generic-framework allowlist.

Preserving project-owned knowledge and authority while replacing runtime coupling strengthens the packaging rule that project-specific canonical and authority material stay outside the generic framework package.

The provenance contract’s non-authoritative, non-Canon rule strengthens the governance runtime proposition by constraining the semantics of the typed content-addressed provenance artifacts it represents.

The architecture separation between reconciliation disposition and separately authorized admission strengthens the reconciliation test boundary in which immutable candidate dispositions fail closed rather than becoming Canon mutation.

The install-package plan’s rule that packaged Steward definitions and executor mechanics acquire no semantic authority strengthens the orchestrator contract’s prohibition on consumers reinterpreting package-owned protocol mechanics as authority.
